items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: Because I joined Dizzy’s band in either the late fifties or the early sixties.

ctx.x: Well I think you had a good positive effect on what he was able to do. Would you agree with that?

Well I’ll tell you, we have to look at that. Because I joined Dizzy’s band in either the late fifties or the early sixties. And the band that I joined was the band with Lee Morgan, Benny Golson, Wynton Kelly, Melba Liston was the musical director, and they were playing so much music man, my head was just — they had my head spinning. I never wrote anything for the band. Because the music that they were playing, the arrangements were so good that I just didn’t feel like I wanted to try to write something coming up…
Yeah. Is there certain things that he liked to hear? Is it possible to answer that? I mean certain tempos, feels? I know he loved Latin grooves.

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah, with Dizzy’s big band. That band was way over my head, but I had to go there anyway.

ctx.x: He’s a monster player. Why’d you leave Maynard Ferguson?
Because I had an opportunity to go with Dizzy, I think.
